title: Regular hyperplane restriction of a free quotient and its Euler difference
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $n\geq1$ and $r\geq1$, put $X=\mathbf P^n_k$, and let
$$0\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r}\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow0$$
be a short exact sequence of coherent modules [pqf-def-coherent]. Use twists $E(d)=E\otimes\mathcal O_X(d)$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], module sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology] and Euler characteristics [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. Let $s\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_X(1))$ be a nonzero linear form such that multiplication $s:F(d-1)\to F(d)$ is injective for every integer $d$. Let $i:H=V(s)\hookrightarrow X$ be its hyperplane closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and fix an identification $H\cong\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$ taking $i^*\mathcal O_X(d)$ to $\mathcal O_H(d)$ for every $d$. Put $K_H=i^*K$ and $F_H=i^*F$, using module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. These modules are coherent and the canonical restricted sequence is short exact:
$$0\longrightarrow K_H\longrightarrow\mathcal O_H^{\oplus r}\longrightarrow F_H\longrightarrow0.$$
For every integer $d$,
$$\chi(H,F_H(d))=\chi(X,F(d))-\chi(X,F(d-1)).$$
In particular, if $P\in\mathbf Q[t]$ satisfies $\chi(X,F(d))=P(d)$ for all integers $d$, then $\chi(H,F_H(d))=P(d)-P(d-1)$ for all integers $d$.

proof.text: The standard affine charts of $X$ and of the given $H\cong\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$ have coordinate rings polynomial in finitely many variables over $k$. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes these rings Noetherian. Thus both schemes are locally Noetherian. By [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], $K,F$ are quasi-coherent of finite type. Pullback preserves these two properties by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] and [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-finite-type]; applying the same coherent criterion on $H$ proves that $K_H,F_H$ are coherent.

source.place: Tag 08AG, first paragraph: coherence of the restricted modules; supporting Tags 00FN, 01XZ, 01BG and 01B6.

proof.text: Write $J$ for the ideal of $H$. On an open trivializing $\mathcal O_X(1)$ write $s=a e$; by [lem-pc-zero-scheme-properties], $J=(a)$ there. The natural quotient formula [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-unit-quotient] identifies $i_*i^*E$ with $E/JE$ for every module $E$. Consequently the restriction maps for $E=K,\mathcal O_X^{\oplus r},F$ are locally reduction modulo $a$, functorially in $E$. For the middle term this identifies the pullback with $\mathcal O_H^{\oplus r}$: on each component $b\otimes c\mapsto bc$, with inverse $c\mapsto1\otimes c$, and these maps glue.

source.place: Tags 08AG and 08A0, local quotient description of the three vertical cokernels; supporting closed-immersion quotient formula 04CJ/08KS.

proof.text: At a stalk on such an open, [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] gives $0\to A\to B\xrightarrow{p} C\to0$, with $A=K_x$, $B=\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\oplus r}$ and $C=F_x$. The hypothesis at $d=1$ is the monomorphism $s:F\to F(1)$; the chosen trivialization of $\mathcal O_X(1)$ identifies its stalk map with multiplication by $a$ on $C$, which is injective by the same stalk theorem. Identify $A$ with its image in $B$ via the injective stalk map. If $u\in A\cap aB$, write $u=ab$. Then $0=p(u)=a p(b)$ implies $p(b)=0$, hence $b\in A$; thus $A\cap aB=aA$. If $p(b)=ac$, lift $c$ to $b'$ and note $b-ab'\in A$. Together with surjectivity of $p$, these two computations prove $0\to A/aA\to B/aB\to C/aC\to0$. The maps in this quotient row are induced by the original stalk maps. The same stalk theorem identifies the stalk of each sheaf quotient $E/aE$ with $E_x/aE_x$. Hence the natural quotient identifications of step 2 identify this quotient row with the stalk row of the canonical restricted maps. For $x=i(h)$ the opens $i^{-1}U$, $U$ a neighbourhood of $x$, are cofinal among neighbourhoods of $h$, so $(i_*E)_x=E_h$. Applying the cited stalkwise criterion on $H$ proves the required short exact sequence.

source.place: Tag 08AG, exact bottom row of the displayed diagram: explicit argument replacing the snake lemma.

proof.text:
For every integer $d$, [def-pc-projective-space-twist] trivializes each twist locally, so tensoring by it preserves exactness and coherence: locally it is the identity functor on modules, and the tensor identifications glue. In particular $F(d-1),F(d)$ and $F_H(d)$ are coherent. The quotient formula in step 2 applied to $F$ gives $\operatorname{Coker}(s:F(-1)\to F)=i_*F_H$: locally both are $F/aF$. Tensor by $\mathcal O_X(d)$. The projection formula in [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology] identifies the last term with $i_*(F_H\otimes i^*\mathcal O_X(d))=i_*F_H(d)$, using the twist identification assumed in the statement. Thus the assumed injectivity gives
$$0\to F(d-1)\xrightarrow{s}F(d)\to i_*F_H(d)\to0.$$
The transitions of the twists identify $\mathcal O(d-1)\otimes\mathcal O(1)$ with $\mathcal O(d)$, so the first map is the stated multiplication by $s$.

source.place: Tag 0EGK (remark-exact-sequence-induction-cohomology), twisting the hyperplane sequence and its projection-formula identification.

proof.text:
The schemes $X=\operatorname{Proj}(k[x_0,\ldots,x_n])$ and $\mathbf P^{n-1}_k=\operatorname{Proj}(k[y_0,\ldots,y_{n-1}])$ of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] are Proj of polynomial rings that are finite-type algebras over their degree-zero part $k$, so their structure morphisms to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are proper by [lem-per-finite-type-graded-proj-proper]; hence $H$ is proper over $k$ through the fixed identification $H\cong\mathbf P^{n-1}_k$. The closed-immersion lemma [lem-pc-closed-immersion-coherent-cohomology], applied to the coherent $F_H(d)$ and the locally Noetherian schemes of step 1, makes $i_*F_H(d)$ coherent and identifies its cohomology with that on $H$. Apply [lem-pc-euler-additive] to the sequence of step 4 on the proper $X$:
$$\chi(X,F(d))=\chi(X,F(d-1))+\chi(X,i_*F_H(d)).$$
The cohomology identification and [def-pc-euler-characteristic] identify the last summand with $\chi(H,F_H(d))$. Subtracting $\chi(X,F(d-1))$ gives the asserted equality for every integer $d$.

source.place: Tags 08AG and 0EGK: hyperplane Euler difference; Euler additivity is Tag 08AA (lemma-euler-characteristic-additive).

proof.text: If $\chi(X,F(t))=P(t)$ for every integer $t$, substitute $t=d$ and $t=d-1$ into the equality of step 5. This gives $\chi(H,F_H(d))=P(d)-P(d-1)$, with no restriction on the sign of $d$.
